source.name: sp_GetInventorySnapshot
source.sourceDefinition:
CREATE PROCEDURE dbo.sp_GetInventorySnapshot
AS
BEGIN
    SET NOCOUNT ON;

    -- Uses NOLOCK hint (dirty reads for performance)
    SELECT
        p.ProductID,
        p.ProductName,
        p.StockQuantity,
        p.Price
    FROM dbo.Products p WITH (NOLOCK)
    WHERE p.StockQuantity > 0
    ORDER BY p.StockQuantity ASC;
END;

result.generatedDdl:
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION dbo.sp_GetInventorySnapshot()
RETURNS TABLE (
    ProductID INTEGER,
    ProductName TEXT,
    StockQuantity INTEGER,
    Price NUMERIC
)
LANGUAGE plpgsql
AS $$
BEGIN
    -- PostgreSQL uses MVCC, no equivalent to NOLOCK needed
    -- Returns result set directly
    RETURN QUERY
    SELECT
        p.ProductID,
        p.ProductName,
        p.StockQuantity,
        p.Price
    FROM dbo.Products p
    WHERE p.StockQuantity > 0
    ORDER BY p.StockQuantity ASC;
END;
$$;
assumptions: ProductID is mapped to INTEGER (assuming SQL Server INT type)
ProductName is mapped to TEXT (assuming SQL Server VARCHAR/NVARCHAR type)
StockQuantity is mapped to INTEGER (assuming SQL Server INT type)
Price is mapped to NUMERIC (assuming SQL Server DECIMAL/NUMERIC/MONEY type)
The dbo schema exists in PostgreSQL or will be created
The Products table structure matches the assumed column types
SET NOCOUNT ON is not needed in PostgreSQL functions (no row count messages by default)
NOLOCK hint removed as PostgreSQL uses MVCC for concurrency control

reviewFlags.reason: Column data types were inferred from common mappings. Verify actual column types in the Products table match the function signature (ProductID, ProductName, StockQuantity, Price types)
Verify that the dbo schema exists in PostgreSQL. PostgreSQL schemas are case-sensitive and may need adjustment
If the original SQL Server Price column uses MONEY or SMALLMONEY, consider using NUMERIC(19,4) or DECIMAL with specific precision/scale

compatibilityNotes.description: SQL Server's NOLOCK hint allows dirty reads (READ UNCOMMITTED). PostgreSQL uses MVCC (Multi-Version Concurrency Control) and does not support dirty reads. The function will use READ COMMITTED isolation by default, which provides consistent snapshots without blocking but cannot read uncommitted data.

SQL Server stored procedure returns result set implicitly. PostgreSQL requires explicit RETURNS TABLE or SETOF declaration. Calling code must use SELECT * FROM sp_GetInventorySnapshot() instead of EXEC sp_GetInventorySnapshot
PostgreSQL functions do not send row count messages by default, so SET NOCOUNT ON is unnecessary and has been removed

The NOLOCK hint in SQL Server was likely used for performance. PostgreSQL's MVCC architecture provides non-blocking reads by default, so performance characteristics should be similar or better without requiring explicit hints
